item.title: 【環境】 Critical dependence of global ocean heat monitoring on the ocean observing system
item.description: International collaboration has facilitated a global ocean observing system, providing data to measure ocean heat content at a resolution that enables the tracking of climate change. This study looks at the contributing nations and the risks to the network under the current political and economic climate.

item.title: 【環境】 The window to avoid locking in decades of steel emissions is closing fast
item.description: Coal-based steel plants risk locking in 60 billion tonnes of CO2 by 2070, but most of these emissions can still be avoided at moderate cost. Steel need not be hard to decarbonize: policymakers must seize the narrow window to redirect investments towards cleaner alternatives this decade.

item.title: 【環境】 Averting the steel carbon lock-in through strategic green investments
item.description: New steel capacity expansion is critical for the feasibility of climate targets, as plants operate for decades. Researchers estimate that while existing and planned plants could commit large emissions, strategic investments using climate finance can largely avert this.

item.title: 【環境】 Improved forest protection at Chinese heritage relic sites
item.description: Deforestation over the past century represents a crucial challenge for biodiversity conservation, but whether biocultural sites can improve conservation outcomes is still unclear. This study examines biocultural sites across China to test how these influence forest conservation outcomes.

item.title: 【環境】 Towards sustainable metal–organic frameworks from lab to practice
item.description: Realistic life-cycle impacts of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are rarely quantified, despite their promise for carbon capture, water treatment, catalysis and other environmental applications. Here we propose a compact, actionable sustainability toolkit for MOFs to systematically verify claims of ‘green’.

item.description: Forest biodiversity is linked, in many cases, to the myriad ecosystem services that support the livelihoods of human populations. Authors here examine the demographic, socioeconomic and institutional variables that impact forest biodiversity across 322 tropical forests.
